q: The Cauchy-Kovalevskaya theorem guarantees local analytic solutions to PDE initial value problems when the data and coefficients are analytic. Its main limitation is:
opts: It requires the domain to be compact
It only applies to linear PDEs
It says nothing about well-posedness in Sobolev spaces (the solution may not be stable in L²)
It only works in one spatial dimension
exp: Cauchy-Kovalevskaya gives local analytic solutions but not stability: small analytic perturbations can lead to wildly different solutions in non-hyperbolic directions (Hadamard's example). Well-posedness in Sobolev spaces requires separate analysis.
